item.title: The maximal margin classifier
item.description:
The maximal margin classifier#

Example: has water been added to the milk?#

Adding water to milk lowers its density (g/mL); lowers its electrical conductivity (mS/cm), because the salts are diluted

item.title: The support vector classifier
item.description:
The support vector classifier#

When the classes overlap#

Real data overlap: no line separates them perfectly

Then the maximal margin classifier has no solution.

Support vector classifier: allow some points inside the street, or on the wrong side of the line, but pay a price for each one

Each point gets a slack variable \(\varepsilon_i\): 0 if it is on the correct side outside the street, between 0 and 1 if inside the street, above 1 if on the wrong side (ISLP 9.2.2).

item.title: Kernels
item.description:
Kernels#

Example: a shaft orbit#

Two proximity probes at right angles measure the position of a rotating shaft (\(x\), \(y\) in \(\mu\)m)

Eddy-current proximity probes are standard on large turbines, compressors and pumps. Plotting \(y\) against \(x\) gives the shaft's orbit.

item.title: SVMs in practice
item.description:
SVMs in practice#

More than two classes#

One-versus-one: fit an SVM for every pair of \(K\) classes: \(K(K - 1)/2\) SVMs. Each votes; the class with the most votes wins. (scikit-learn's SVC does this.)

One-versus-all: fit \(K\) SVMs: each class against all the others. Choose the class whose SVM is most confident

Fault type: three classes (imbalance, misalignment, bearing wear): 3 SVMs either way

\(3 \times 2/2 = 3\) pairs; and 3 one-versus-all SVMs. With 10 classes it would be 45 against 10.
